summary: Glimepiride is a once-daily sulfonylurea that improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes by stimulating insulin secretion. Started at 1-2 mg with the first meal, titrated to a maximum of 8 mg daily. Main risk is hypoglycemia, greatest in the elderly and renally impaired.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

dosage.d: Start 1-2 mg once daily; usual maintenance 1-4 mg; max 8 mg/day
Start 1 mg once daily, titrate slowly
1-2 mg once daily with the other agent

admin: Take once daily with breakfast or the first main meal
Do not skip meals after dosing - risk of hypoglycemia
Titrate dose no more often than every 1-2 weeks
Use 1 mg start in elderly or renal impairment
Educate on recognizing and treating hypoglycemia
moa: Stimulates insulin release from functioning pancreatic beta cells by binding the sulfonylurea receptor (SUR1) on the ATP-sensitive potassium channel, causing channel closure, membrane depolarization, calcium influx and insulin exocytosis. Requires residual beta-cell function.
preg: Not recommended. Insulin is preferred for glycemic control in pregnancy. Sulfonylureas near term may cause prolonged neonatal hypoglycemia.
lact: Not recommended due to potential neonatal hypoglycemia; discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Increased hypoglycemia risk; start at 1 mg once daily and titrate carefully based on glucose. Avoid in severe impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution; start low and titrate slowly. Impaired metabolism increases hypoglycemia risk.

major: Other glucose-lowering agents (insulin, sulfonylureas) - additive hypoglycemia
Concurrent strong CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) - increased glimepiride levels and hypoglycemia
moderate: Beta-blockers - mask hypoglycemia symptoms and impair recovery
NSAIDs, sulfonamides, salicylates, warfarin - potentiate hypoglycemia (protein displacement)
Thiazides, corticosteroids, sympathomimetics - hyperglycemia / reduced effect
Colesevelam - reduced glimepiride exposure (take glimepiride >=4 h before)
minor: Cimetidine, ranitidine - possible altered glucose response
ACE inhibitors - may enhance glucose lowering
interactions.food: Take with first meal; high-fat meals slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; potentiates hypoglycemia and rarely causes disulfiram-like reaction.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers blood glucose; may affect glucose-tolerance testing.

monitoring: Fasting blood glucose and HbA1c periodically
CBC if signs of blood dyscrasia
counsel: Take with breakfast/first meal; never skip meals after dosing
Recognize and treat hypoglycemia (carry fast-acting glucose)
Continue diet, exercise and glucose self-monitoring
pk: Store at 20-25 C, protect from light and moisture
pearls: Once-daily dosing with lower hypoglycemia risk than glyburide
Start 1 mg in elderly/renal impairment to limit hypoglycemia
Weight gain common; pair with lifestyle measures
missed: If a meal is missed, skip that dose. If remembered with the meal, take it; do not double the dose to make up.
overdose: Can cause severe, prolonged hypoglycemia. Treat conscious patients with oral glucose; severe cases need IV dextrose and close monitoring (recurrence over 24-48 h). Glucagon if needed. Octreotide may help refractory sulfonylurea hypoglycemia. Hospitalize.
